timing_lunar_solar: Celebrated throughout the year (often post-harvest or upon vow fulfillment)
variety_or_region: Universal Gaddi Festival (Chamba, Kangra, Doda, Kathua, Udhampur)
purpose_and_significance: The premier religious and social ceremony of the Gaddi people. An all-night thanksgiving ritual dedicated to Lord Shiva to express gratitude for prosperity, recovery from sickness, successful sheep transhumance, or family milestones.
associated_rituals: Suspension of the floral garland (Mala Mundan)
Singing of Ainchali ballads throughout the night
source_citation: Chakraborty (2024), Section: Religious Life; Shashi (1977), pp. 65-72; Kumar (2019)

variety_or_region: Bharmaur, Chamba, Himachal Pradesh (draws pilgrims from across J&K and HP)
purpose_and_significance: Annual high-altitude sacred pilgrimage to Lake Manimahesh (4,080 meters) at the base of Mount Manimahesh Kailash (5,653 meters). Gaddi pilgrims take a holy dip in the icy glacial waters (Dal) facing the sacred peak, seeking divine liberation and blessings for their flocks.
associated_rituals: Trek from Bharmaur via Hadsar and Dhancho
Holy dip in the Dal Lake
source_citation: Chakraborty (2024), Section: Manimahesh Pilgrimage; Shashi (1977); PLSI Vol. 12 (2014)

timing_lunar_solar: First day of Vaisakha month (April 13/14 solar transition)
variety_or_region: Chamba, Kangra, and Jammu Gaddi settlements
purpose_and_significance: Spring festival marking the solar new year and the commencement of seasonal pastoral transhumance. Shepherds prepare equipment, inspect flocks, and offer prayers for safe journeys up into high pastures.

variety_or_region: Chamba, Kangra, Mandi, and Jammu foothills
purpose_and_significance: Autumn harvest festival marking the end of the rainy season and the joyful return of Gaddi shepherds from the high alpine meadows down to the village valleys.
associated_rituals: Distribution of fresh green maize cobs and walnuts
Barber offering looking-glass to elders for blessings

purpose_and_significance: Historic monsoon festival celebrating agricultural abundance. Participants pin golden silk tassels representing maize blossoms (minjar) to their cholas and float offerings in the sacred Ravi river.
associated_rituals: Tying silk minjar tassels to garments
Shobha Yatra procession to the Ravi river

timing_lunar_solar: Last day of Pausha month / 1st of Magha (mid-January)
purpose_and_significance: Midwinter festival celebrating the winter solstice and the lengthening of days. Families gather around night bonfires in sub-zero weather, dancing and singing traditional Gaddi songs.
associated_rituals: Preparing khichdi with black gram and ghee
Offering sesame seeds and puffed rice to the flame
